problem: Existing world action models (WAMs) either generate future observations autoregressively/by joint denoising at test time (high latency) or tightly couple video and action modeling, so high-dimensional visual generation noise interferes with the low-dimensional action space and hurts planning and generalization.
motivation: Embodied navigation ultimately needs actions; future prediction should be an auxiliary training signal, not an inference-time burden. Decoupling the two distributions while still letting video supervision shape the action representation could give both accuracy and real-time efficiency for driving and urban navigation.
key_idea: Use a Mixture-of-Transformers with a video generation expert (Wan2.2-5B) and a small action expert, linked by an asymmetric attention mask (video tokens see action tokens, not vice versa), so video is jointly trained but skipped at inference.
insight: Joint training with video generation helps the action expert even though video is dropped at test time (w/o co-train 87.4/87.9 vs w/ co-train 89.1/89.5 PDMS/EPDMS). Asymmetric masking beats both full joint attention (87.4 EPDMS, 28.0 navhard) and fully isolated attention (88.3, 29.4) at 320x384, reaching 88.8 / 31.6. Larger VGE and AE capacity help most on the harder navhard benchmark, and action-only inference gives up to ~8x speedup at almost no loss (0.17 s vs 1.38 s).
method: Problem formulation: future frames are used only as training supervision; inference models a ~ p(a | z(o_t,l)) from a single backbone forward pass with no future video generation.

MoT architecture: video generation expert (VGE) from Wan2.2-5B, reusing its video VAE and T5 text encoder, plus an action expert (AE) implemented as a DiT with the same depth but hidden dim 1024 (~1B params; total ~6B); all tokens cross-attend to language and interact in a shared latent space via expert-specific projections, FFNs and heads.
Agent state encoder: encodes ego state and combines it with the language instruction to condition the model.

Asymmetric attention mask: action tokens attend only to current-observation tokens; future video tokens attend to current-observation and action tokens; the reverse is masked, so the video branch can be dropped at inference without a train/inference mismatch.
Flow-matching objective: L = L_act + λ L_video (λ=1), both as velocity-field regression; the video loss is conditioned on the action tokens and its gradients flow into the AE.

Inference: only current observation and action tokens are used with 10 denoising steps, CFG 1.0 (2 steps in the latency setting); front camera only; action horizon 8 for NAVSIM, 5 for CityWalker; best-of-N=6 variant optional.

setting.backbone: Wan2.2-5B video generation expert + ~1B action-expert DiT (Mixture-of-Transformers, fine-tuned/trained)
setting.training_data: NAVSIM navtrain (1,192 scenarios) for NAVSIM; CityWalker 6 h fine-tuning split (of 15 h NYC teleop data); Wan2.2 pretrained priors; no RL or auxiliary datasets
setting.observation: monocular front-facing RGB (plus ego state and text instruction)
setting.action_space: predicted waypoint trajectories: 8 waypoints (x,y,θ) at 0.5 s for NAVSIM; 5 waypoints (x,y) for CityWalker; a PD controller converts them to velocity for the Go2
setting.simulator: NAVSIM-v2 (navhard with 3DGS synthetic stage) / NAVSIM-v1 (navtest), CityWalker dataset offline evaluation

numbers_note: Real-robot results (Unitree Go2, indoor and outdoor zero-shot) are only qualitative figures. The navhard/navtest benchmarks are not in the canonical list, hence 'other:'; the split is recorded as 'test' since NAVSIM navhard/navtest are the official test-style benchmarks. Latency table: Metis 0.17 s (action-only, 2 steps, RTX 4090; PDMS 88.9, EPDMS 89.2) vs 1.38 s with video.
results: Metis reaches EPDMS 32.2 on navhard (best in both stages, vs SimScale-style baselines ≤27.5 such as DiffusionDrive 27.5), 89.5 on navtest (90.3 with best-of-6) versus the best prior DriveFine 87.1 (VLA) and DriveVLA-W0 86.1 (WAM), and 89.1/89.7 PDMS on NAVSIM-v1. On CityWalker it beats all fine-tuned baselines (All L2 0.64 vs CityWalker 1.07, MAOE 9.8 vs 11.5), while the large-scale-pretrained ABot-N0 still has lower overall MAOE (7.6).
limitations: Relies heavily on a pretrained video generation expert; training remains computationally expensive, and the VAE downsampling ratio affects the efficiency/quality trade-off.
Monocular front-camera input causes deviations in long-horizon planning in open-world scenes; reliability in extreme corner cases is not validated.
Real-world deployment is only shown qualitatively, with no quantitative real-robot success metrics.
